headline.headline: RAFAELA GOES DEEP THREE STRAIGHT AS RED SOX SWEEP DODGERS
headline.deck: Boston outfielder's home run streak powers 8-4 victory over Los Angeles
headline.body:
BOSTON -- Ceddanne Rafaela homered for the third consecutive game Sunday as the Boston Red Sox closed out an 8-4 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers to complete a three-game sweep, delivering one of the most electric individual stretches by a Red Sox hitter this summer.

Rafaela's back-to-back-to-back long ball sequence against one of baseball's marquee franchises instantly elevated the young center fielder into the conversation as one of the American League's most dangerous threats entering August. The Dodgers, built around a roster loaded with star power, had no answer for him across the entire series.

The sweep is a statement for Boston, which entered August chasing position in the AL East standings. Taking three straight from Los Angeles in high-profile fashion sends a clear signal that the Red Sox intend to be heard in the playoff race. Rafaela's bat will be the name to watch as the calendar turns.

secondary.headline: SCHERZER STANDS TALL AS CARDS ERUPT LATE TO STUN BLUE JAYS
secondary.deck: St. Louis scores four in the ninth to turn a tight game into a 5-1 road win
secondary.body:
TORONTO -- Max Scherzer earned the victory Sunday as the St. Louis Cardinals held Toronto scoreless through seven innings and then buried the Blue Jays with a four-run ninth to complete a 5-1 road win before 41,321 at Rogers Centre. Lars Nootbaar and Julian Urías each doubled, and the Cardinals received a three-base hit from George Springer that kept the Toronto offense off balance all afternoon.

The game was a masterpiece of patience. St. Louis scratched out a single run in the third and then played lockdown baseball until the roof caved in during the ninth. Toronto managed only one run, coming in the eighth inning, before the Cardinals sealed it. The win in 2 hours and 34 minutes underscored how efficiently Scherzer and the St. Louis bullpen can suffocate an opponent when working with even the slimmest of leads.

secondary.headline: DONOVAN MITCHELL MARRIES COCO JONES IN GREENWICH CEREMONY
secondary.deck: Cleveland star and R&B singer exchange vows at weekend wedding in Connecticut
secondary.body:
GREENWICH, Conn. -- Cleveland Guardians star Donovan Mitchell and singer Coco Jones were married over the weekend in a ceremony held in Greenwich, Connecticut, with the couple's first dance set to Musiq Soulchild's 2000 hit 'Love.' Video posted by the couple's representatives showed a celebration that drew widespread attention across professional sports and entertainment circles.

Mitchell, one of the NBA's premier shooting guards and a central figure in Cleveland's playoff push through the conference semifinals, has been among the league's most visible personalities off the court this summer. The wedding comes during a busy NBA offseason period, with free agency signings and extensions dominating league news alongside the conference semifinals still in progress.

secondary.headline: MERRILL CLEARS THE FENCE AS PADRES EDGE GIANTS 5-4
secondary.deck: Jackson Merrill's homer and clutch RBIs from Cronenworth and Campusano lift San Diego
secondary.body:
SAN DIEGO -- Jackson Merrill homered and Jake Cronenworth and Luis Campusano each drove in a run as the San Diego Padres held off the San Francisco Giants 5-4 Sunday in a tight National League West battle. The one-run margin made every at-bat count, and the Padres found just enough offense to protect a lead that never felt entirely secure.

Merrill has emerged as one of San Diego's most reliable run producers this season, and his home run Sunday served as the decisive blow in a game where neither side could establish comfortable separation. Cronenworth and Campusano provided the supporting production that proved essential. The win keeps the Padres pressing forward in a crowded NL West race heading into August.

column.headline: RAFAELA IS THE REAL DEAL, AND THE DODGERS JUST FOUND OUT THE HARD WAY
column.body:
There are moments in a baseball season when a young player stops being a prospect and starts being a problem for everyone else in the league. Ceddanne Rafaela reached that moment this weekend. Homering in three straight games against the Los Angeles Dodgers -- a team that arrived in Boston as the glamour franchise of the sport -- is not a small thing. That is a declaration. The rest of the AL East would be wise to take note.

The Dodgers came into Fenway with star power and left with a sweep on their record and questions about how to defend a hitter who is clearly growing into something special. August is when pennant races sharpen and reputations get built. Rafaela has done more in three games to announce himself than most players manage in an entire month. Keep his name close. He is going to matter in October.

story.headline: HARPER BLAST, SHUTOUT SILENCE BIRDS AS PHILLIES BLANK ORIOLES 8-0
story.deck: Philadelphia erupts for six runs across two innings, Backhus cruises in Camden Yards rout.
story.body:
BALTIMORE, Aug. 2 — Bryce Harper crushed his 23rd home run of the season and Philadelphia's pitching staff never gave the Orioles a breath, as the Phillies rolled to an 8-0 shellacking at Camden Yards Sunday in a game completed in 1 hour and 54 minutes despite a 2-hour, 17-minute delay. Starter Backhus worked through a Baltimore lineup that stranded nine baserunners but could not dent the scoreboard in any of its nine innings, leaving the Orioles' Kyle Bradish tagged with the loss.

Philadelphia built its margin steadily and decisively. The Phillies scratched out two runs in the third inning, added one more in the fifth, then blew the game open with a three-run sixth that put the contest firmly out of reach. Harper's homer and a two-run shot by Cruz — his second of the year — provided the power, while Crawford contributed a double to a Philadelphia attack that left 10 runners on base before an announced crowd of 31,403.

The victory kept Philadelphia relevant in the National League East race, where the Phillies sit at 59-53, four games behind the division lead. The Nationals visit Citizens Bank Park on Monday looking to snap a road slide, giving Philadelphia a chance to build on a dominant performance that saw them post their most lopsided result in recent weeks.

story.headline: MITCHELL SAYS 'I DO,' MAVS LOCK UP MARSHALL, AND WARRIORS RELOAD IN BUSY NBA OFFSEASON
story.deck: Dallas secures Marshall for three years while Golden State brings back two familiar faces
story.body:
The NBA offseason rolled on Sunday with a flurry of moves and milestones, none more personal than Cleveland Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell exchanging vows with singer and actress Coco Jones in a Greenwich, Connecticut ceremony Saturday. The couple shared their first dance to Musiq Soulchild's 2000 R&B classic 'Love,' a moment captured in a video posted by those close to the couple. Mitchell, who averaged 26.5 points per game last season, became one of the league's most celebrated athletes off the court as well as on it.

On the business front, the Dallas Mavericks moved swiftly to secure one of their core pieces, extending forward Naji Marshall on a three-year, $52.2 million deal that will keep him in Dallas through the 2029-30 season. Marshall, 26, emerged as a reliable two-way contributor for Dallas and the extension signals the franchise's commitment to building around a core that can compete in the Western Conference for years to come. The deal rewards a player who elevated his game considerably during the Mavericks' playoff runs.

In Golden State, the Warriors continued their methodical roster reconstruction by bringing back forward Gary Payton II on a one-year, $3.9 million veteran minimum contract, reuniting him with a franchise where he won a championship in 2022. Draymond Green also finalized his return to the Warriors on a new deal, anchoring Golden State's defense once again alongside Stephen Curry. Oklahoma City's Chet Holmgren, meanwhile, addressed reporters about the Thunder's roster departures, calling the exits 'part of the business of this game' as the young center braces for an even larger leadership role heading into next season.

story.headline: SHARKS LOCK UP GRAF, PENGUINS EXTEND NOVAK AS NHL SUMMER ROSTER MOVES HEAT UP
story.deck: San Jose and Pittsburgh make key forward commitments while Sweden's Färjestad rescinds Foote deal.
story.body:
The San Jose Sharks secured one of their most promising young forwards Monday, re-signing Collin Graf to a three-year contract worth $12.75 million. Graf, 24, delivered a breakout campaign last season with 21 goals and 25 assists across 81 games, establishing himself as a cornerstone piece for a Sharks franchise still rebuilding toward contention. The deal carries an average annual value of $4.25 million and keeps Graf in teal through the 2028-29 season.

In Pittsburgh, the Penguins moved to retain dependable forward Tommy Novak on a three-year extension, betting on his steady two-way play as the franchise navigates a transitional era following the retirement of Sidney Crosby. Novak, known for his reliability on the penalty kill and consistent puck possession, gives Pittsburgh a trustworthy middle-six presence as general manager Kyle Dubas continues reshaping the roster around younger talent.

Meanwhile, controversy erupted overseas when Swedish Elite League club Färjestad BK announced it would not honor the previously agreed contract of defenseman Cal Foote following significant fan backlash. The IIHF added to a turbulent Monday by confirming Russia remains barred from four major tournaments in 2027, a continuation of sanctions stemming from the ongoing geopolitical conflict that has kept Russian clubs and national teams sidelined from international competition.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are reshaping their rosters around new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market, with teams across the league scrambling to secure their next franchise signal-caller following a winter of high-profile retirements and contract disputes. The Cleveland Browns, fresh off another disappointing campaign, are reportedly in advanced talks to trade for a veteran starter, while the New York Giants have already committed to rebuilding around 2026 first-round pick phenom Marcus Harwell, the mobile quarterback out of Tennessee who dazzled scouts at the combine with a 4.47 forty and a cannon arm that drew comparisons to a young Josh Allen.

On the free-agent front, veteran wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins, seeking one final shot at a championship, signed a one-year prove-it deal with the Kansas City Chiefs, pairing him with Patrick Mahomes in what analysts are calling the most dangerous offensive duo assembled this offseason. Meanwhile, the Dallas Cowboys made waves by releasing aging cornerback Trevon Diggs and immediately redirecting that cap space toward a blockbuster extension for young pass rusher Micah Parsons, locking up the defensive star through the 2030 season.

Draft analysts are still dissecting April's seven-round selection process, with the consensus view that the Las Vegas Raiders landed the steal of the draft in third-round linebacker Darius Cole out of Georgia, a sideline-to-sideline tackler who ran a blazing 4.41 at the combine. Training camps are not scheduled to open until late July, but coaching staffs are already installing new systems, and several teams including the Seattle Seahawks and Carolina Panthers have announced significant scheme changes that figure to reshape their identities heading into the 2026 season.
